hypothesis.action: introduce a first-class third execution-provenance for 'the calling session is the named worker', decomposed into bounded phases whose solution shapes are decided per-phase (frame does NOT pick the solution)
hypothesis.users: operators running Nexus local_provider + primary_provider=claude from inside an active Claude Code session (the majority Nexus environment)
hypothesis.outcome: complete the governed lifecycle in-session without fabricating provenance; /review and /ship can distinguish attested from spawned execution
hypothesis.evidence: idea-brief Sources 1/2/4/6 show fabrication is forced by the absent concept (not operator error); three grounded independent reviews established the concept must be modeled across schema+ownership+review-contract, not patched

success_criteria: Session-is-worker /build produces an artifact whose execution provenance is a schema-enforced discriminator (not an operator-typed string); schema rejects an attested artifact missing it; attested vs spawned distinguishable by one typed field, not prose.

Completing a session-is-worker /build requires zero hand-fabrication of dispatch_command/receipt/actual_route; the attested path has a defined writer such that those are legitimately absent and schema still validates.

/review over an attested build neither crashes (review.ts:541 null actual_route, :1084 null deref) nor silently passes the provenance gate it should not (review.ts:1188 / build.ts:107 fix-cycle eligibility); it yields a defined non-degraded verdict.
The trust anchor references something the attesting session did not author; forging/removing it causes /review or /ship to reject or downgrade.
The milestone roadmap decomposes Problem A into >=3 dependency-ordered phases, each independently frame-able; no phase is 'design the whole model'; order justified by dependency not convenience.
non_goals: NOT picking the solution in this frame (no operator_attested-as-schema, no trust-anchor mechanism, no specific review.ts edits) - per-phase decisions; pre-deciding repeats the verified v1.2 failure.
NOT Problems B (streaming parity) or C (lifecycle re-entry) - independent, separately routed.
NOT changing governed_ccb or non-claude/non-single-host dispatch.
NOT retroactively re-running historical fabricated artifacts (novelWriter SP2 + prior); migration is a phase question, not a precondition.
NOT a point release - explicitly not packageable as a hotfix.
out_of_scope: Problem B and Problem C (separately routed; operator might assume the silent agent_team gap or frame->discover rejection are included - they are not).
The novelWriter SP2 historical run (stays committed/disclosed; not retroactively fixed or re-graded).
governed_ccb provenance records (CCB dispatch is out).
A specific provenance_kind field name/schema (deliberately NOT specified - the disproven solutioning-in-disguise).
acceptance_criteria: Given an operator in a Claude Code session local_provider/claude who did the implementation in-session, when they complete the governed /build, then the artifact carries a schema-enforced session-attested provenance discriminator, no fabricated dispatch/receipt fields, schema passes.

Given a session-attested build artifact (discriminator set, actual_route legitimately absent), when /review runs, then it neither throws on the null route nor records provenance_consistent in a way that silently grants undue fix-cycle eligibility; it produces a defined verdict appropriate to attested provenance.

Given this milestone frame is approved, when the roadmap is created, then Problem A is decomposed into >=3 dependency-ordered phases, the first being the ownership-model question (status.json/ledger writer when nothing spawns), and no phase's scope is 'design the entire model'.
open_questions_to_plan: Phase 1 boundary: is it scoped as 'frame the ownership model and decide if it is bounded' (a decision-gate phase) rather than 'implement it'? /plan sequences, does not answer the ownership question here.
Phase count and dependency spine: ownership model -> provenance carrier -> /review contract -> trust anchor -> (optional) migration. /plan proposes; each phase gets its own /frame.
Milestone gate: commit to phases 2+ only after Phase 1's frame proves bounded (Risk 5).
Independent-review gate placement: after this milestone frame (before /plan) and after each phase frame - recorded, not skipped.
Hard deferral (must NOT leak into planning as pre-decided): provenance field shape, trust-anchor mechanism, exact review.ts edits, migration policy - the codex-flagged relapse vector.

provenance.supersedes: v1.1.x-hotfix and v1.2-single-concept framings (disproven records, retained on-branch)
provenance.scope_class: milestone; not point release; solution explicitly deferred to per-phase frames
provenance.review_gate: requires independent grounded review before /plan (session iron rule: 3x applied, 3x caught a blocker)
